description:
PERF (s517c, perf round 47 member 4, FILED -- under the 15 % bar).  lcbytes (bench row 332, `lc($s) . uc($s) . ucfirst($s)` over 200 UTF-8 byte strings, 3.0x perl).

Profile (s517c tree): %p-case-map-ascii 13.6 %, sb-kernel:ub32-bash-copy 11.6, %p-concat-2 11.1, %p-utf8-bytes-scan 11.1, %p-bytes-look-utf8-p 4.0, p-ucfirst 7.6 cum.

Hand-replaced A/B (scratch/s517c/hr-jl2.log, whole process, median of 7, load ~1.9; levers in the s517c worktree scratch/s517c/prof/leverL1.lisp, leverL2.lisp):
  lb (base)        1.247 s
  +L1              1.175 s  (-5.8 %)  a compiler macro on p-. that turns a left-nested chain (p-. (p-. a b) c) into ONE pre-sized %p-concat-3 when all three are strings (evaluation order kept: a, b, then c; the a.b concat of two strings is unobservable so it may wait); emission is nested p-. today, not p-string-concat.
  +L2              1.240 s  (-0.6 %)  ucfirst/lcfirst's Unicode arm = one copy + one char set instead of concatenate + two subseq.
  +L1+L2           1.149 s  (-7.9 %)
Not shipped: under 15 %.  Not tried: the per-call UTF-8 validation (%p-utf8-bytes-scan) runs once for lc and again for uc on the same string -- the "is this undecoded bytes" answer would belong on the value (#1389's per-scalar flag), which PCL does not keep; a one-entry eq memo is unsafe while simple strings can be mutated in place.

The regime PCL implements (asked by the brief): under /d (no unicode_strings) a string whose chars >= 0x80 all sit in well-formed UTF-8 sequences is BYTES and gets ASCII rules; any other string gets Unicode rules; under :u always Unicode.  Probe scratch/s517c/pr/m4.pl: perl differs on a native high-byte string that is NOT valid UTF-8 ("\xC9cole": perl leaves \xC9, PCL lowercases to \xE9 -- not-supported.md "The per-scalar UTF-8 flag") and on Unicode special casing (#1036).
subject: lcbytes: a 3-way . chain concat + a cheaper ucfirst arm are -7.9 % whole run (FILED, under the 15 % bar)
